# FDG7008

> DO NOT have public members that return exceptions as the return value or an `out` parameter.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 7.1 Exception Throwing.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (full coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG7008
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application none, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Throw the exception instead of returning it from '{0}'

Library only: the text scopes it to public members. FDG7008 reports an externally visible method whose return type, or the type of one of its out parameters, is System.Exception or derives from it. Overrides and interface implementations are not reported (Exception.GetBaseException is an override target), nor properties: the text and its DoSomething example concern the return value of a call, and an exception property such as InnerException is the extra information FDG7060 asks for. Exception builder methods (FDG7009) are not reported when they are not externally visible, as in the body of FDG7009. Changing the return type changes the public signature, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

Returning exceptions from public APIs instead of throwing them defeats many of the benefits of exception-based error reporting.

```csharp
// bad design
public Exception DoSomething() { ... }
```
